mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to higher borrowing costs and reduced business investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over the last quarter signals a weakening demand environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in the last two months signals supply chain disruptions and reduced output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in the last month, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% and retail sales (RSAFS) decrease by more than 1% in the last two months, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% and RSAFS decreases > 1% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% over the last three months signals inflationary pressures, which leads to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is growing at less than 1% year-over-year and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy combined with weak supply-side growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of INDPRO growth and FEDFUNDS level on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
